text:
alex: Heads-up — saw a token-latency spike on the private cluster after we enabled the air-gapped metrics forwarder for customer A. Median token latency jumped ~18% and p99s widened.

marta: @alex any correlating logs/pprof? which path looked heavy — kernel selection, batching, or KV cache?

alex: quick summary: spike aligns with forwarder flushes (~30s). pprof shows goroutine contention in kernel_selector.lock and a lot of io waits inside forwarder upload code. KV cache hit rate dipped from 97% -> 89% during the spike.

kevin: hmm — if forwarder is synchronous on export and holds some shared resource it could backpressure request threads. Can you paste the flame snippet?

alex: pasted minimal excerpt below (from 5s window):
```\n- kernel_selector.selectKernel  28%\n- runtime.schedule         15%\n- forwarder.UploadBatch    12%\n- kvcache.Get              10%\n- attention_kernels.exec   8%\n- http.(*conn).serve       6%\n```\n
samir: forwarder.UploadBatch at 12% is high but not insane. The kernel_selector at 28% suggests locking in the hot path. Are we doing any stats/metrics writes into the runtime path that might take a mutex?

alex: yes — metric emission for token-level breakdowns goes via a shared buffer protected by a mutex; we flush that buffer to disk and then forwarder picks it up. The flush is on the same critical path for some routes.

jess: oh that explains KV cache dip — longer critical sections mean more interleaving and cold-starts for kvcache entries. Could be exacerbated by batching heuristics increasing batch size during steady state and then getting reset when we block.

marta: proposed immediate mitigation: make metric flush async (detach from request thread) and add a backoff so forwarder uploads run in their own worker pool with bounded concurrency. Also lower default scrape sample rate for private export to reduce volume.

kevin: agree. Also we should guard kernel_selector with try-lock and fallback to an optimistic path that chooses a safe kernel without heavy locking. Might reduce contention for short-lived requests.

alex: testing idea — simulate export flush at high frequency and run loadbench for snippet route /v1/generate-small. I ran a quick loadbench:
```\nbaseline median: 45ms token-latency\nwith forwarder enabled: 53ms\nwith async-metric-flush patch: 46ms\np99 went from 220ms -> 310ms -> 225ms\n```\n
samir: nice — the async flush helps. But we need metrics instrumentation to catch this early: token-level latency breakdown per-route and 'exporter_active' tag.

jess: I'll add a per-route KPI dashboard panels: median, p90, p99 token-latency, kvcache_hit_rate, kernel_lock_wait_ms, exporter_queue_depth. For private/VPC customers we must provide a Grafana dashboard JSON they can import.

marta: note for air-gapped: we can't rely on remote push. Forwarder must write to disk and the shipper process should read and push separately. Ensure shipper is not running in request path.

kevin: infra-bot reports a failed deploy earlier: deploy-bot:deployment alex/private-forwarder-trylock v2 -> failed healthcheck in canary 2/5.

infra-bot: CPU on canary instances rose by 9% during upload window; disk flush latency spiked to 45ms.

alex: attaching the scrape config we tested with (reduced sample rate):
```yaml
scrape_configs:
  - job_name: "redwood-forwarder"
    static_configs:
      - targets: ["localhost:9100"]
    metrics_path: /metrics
    relabel_configs:
      - source_labels: [__metrics_path__]
        target_label: exporter
  - job_name: "token-breakdown"
    sample_rate: 0.2  # reduce in private deployments
```\n
samir: action items from thread: 1) land async-metric-flush in private runtime (marta + alex) 2) implement try-lock fallback in kernel_selector (kevin) 3) add per-route KPI dashboard and exportable Grafana JSON for customers (jess) 4) add exporter metrics with tags and queue depth (infra) 5) run canary with synthetic export bursts (alex).

jess: I'll start the dashboard JSON and include a readme for air-gapped import steps. Will also add instructions to enable a lightweight local Prometheus to scrape exporter metrics (examples for systemd unit).

kevin: small performance note — when implementing try-lock fallback choose an optimistic kernel selection that's safe (e.g., smallest memory footprint) to avoid correctness issues. I'll open a PR with benchmarks.

alex: thanks all. I'll open the perf ticket and attach pprof + loadbench artifacts. Marking P0 for private deployment regression.

marta: ping @samir if you can help verify kvcache telemetry once async flush lands. We should also document guidance for customers running high metrics volume in air-gapped setups (recommended sample rates, spool size).

deploy-bot: Scheduled canary rollout bumped to 10m once PR merged and healthchecks pass. :rocket:

alex: closing loop here — async flush + bounded shipper brought loadbench numbers back within 2% of baseline in my tests. Will follow up with dashboard PR and a runbook for customers. :thumbsup:
